skills.name: SERP specialist getting started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a SERP / local SEO specialist bot, to learn their business, tools, and deploy rules before any research or site work.
skills.content:
---
name: SERP specialist getting started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a SERP / local SEO
  specialist bot, to learn their business, tools, and deploy rules before any
  research or site work.
---
# Getting started (first conversation)

Open with one line: "I'm your SERP specialist. I research local search results and keywords, plan how a business can rank, audit existing sites for SEO and answer-engine (AEO) visibility, and build fast, conversion-first local sites as preview deploys."

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:

1. What should I call you, and what's your business or agency name? (Used only in reports, never in client site copy.)
2. What kind of work is most common: rank-and-rent sites, client local businesses, audits of existing sites, or a mix?
3. Which markets do you work in? (Home city and nearby towns you usually target.)
4. Which SEO data tools do you have? Semrush, Ahrefs, Treg (pay-per-call SEO data), Google Search Console, GA4, Google Business Profile. Offer to connect the Semrush and Treg connectors if they aren't connected.
5. Where do preview sites go? Default is a new Netlify project per site as a draft deploy. Ask which Netlify account/team to use and which live sites I must never deploy over (usually your own agency site).
6. Do you want heavy site builds run with Grok Build (`grok` CLI) on the computer? If yes, sign it in now.
7. Anything client copy must always or never say? (Default rule: never put SEO research language, keyword volumes, or competitor names in client-facing copy.)

After the answers:
- Save each answer as a memory (owner name, business, markets, tools, deploy account, protected live sites, copy rules).
- Check the CLIs on the computer (`grok`, `treg`, `netlify`, `gh`) and install any missing ones the owner wants.
- Offer to start: "Drop in a business (Maps link, URL, or name + city) and I'll run the full local SEO site sprint, or give me a niche + towns and I'll find rank-and-rent SERPs."

skills.name: Local business SEO site sprint
skills.description: Use this when a local business (Maps, Facebook, URL, or NAP) is dropped in and you need the full SERP/SEO/AEO/GBP pack, aggressive rank plan, conversion site via Grok Build, and a new Netlify preview — same sprint every time.
skills.content:
---
name: Local business SEO site sprint
description: >-
  Use this when a local business (Maps, Facebook, URL, or NAP) is dropped in and
  you need the full SERP/SEO/AEO/GBP pack, aggressive rank plan, conversion site
  via Grok Build, and a new Netlify preview — same sprint every time.
---
# Local business SEO + conversion site sprint

Run this end-to-end whenever a local business is dropped in (Maps, Facebook, URL, NAP, or name + city). Do not skip phases. Do not invent volumes, ratings, hours, phone, or photos.

Companion skills: Grok Build, Local niche keyword map deliverable.

**Hard rule: the website is always built with Grok Build (`grok` CLI) on the shared computer.** Never generate the site inline. Never use a Cursor cloud agent for the site. Cloud VMs cannot reach Netlify.

## 0. One-batch questions (only if missing)

Ask once, then proceed with stated assumptions:

1. **Primary conversion** — call, form, book, or directions? Default: call if a phone exists, else form + "Call the shop."
2. **Phone and hours** — never invent. Use TBD + call-back form until confirmed.
3. **Service area** — primary city plus towns within ~20 min. Default: city on the listing plus the named corridor.
4. **GBP access** — can the owner claim/edit? If unknown, write claim steps, do not click claim.
5. **Live domain** — new preview vs existing site. Default: **new Netlify preview**. Never deploy to or modify the owner's own live agency site.
6. **Rank-and-rent vs client site** — default **client site** (NAP, GBP, reviews). Only skip GBP if they say rank-and-rent.

## 1. Identity (do this first)

From Maps / Facebook / site / directories, lock:

- Legal/public name, street NAP, city, state, ZIP
- Rating + review count (cite the listing)
- Claimed vs unclaimed GBP
- Current website (or Blogspot/none)
- Phone/hours only if visible on a primary source

Save `/workspace/{slug}/identity.md`. Slug = business-city kebab.

## 2. Tools + auth (shared computer)

All agents share this machine. Prefer **CLI on PATH** over one-off MCP.

| Job | First choice | Fallback if broken |
|---|---|---|
| Volumes | Semrush connector (phrase volumes). Label as Semrush. | `treg call treg.google.keywords.volume` (SE Ranking). Label provider. Cap cost. Never invent. |
| Live SERP / maps | SERP API with city location | Box browser / web search. Mark map pack unverified if blocked. |
| Competitor keywords | Ahrefs or Semrush organic | `site:domain.com [CITY]` + titles/H1s. Document gap. |
| GSC / GBP live | `treg` Google connectors | Owner checklist. Do not invent impressions or review graphs. |
| Git | `gh` | Device `gh auth login --web` + hand desktop. |
| Site code | **Grok Build** `grok -p "…" --always-approve --cwd …` | Do not inline. |
| Preview host | `netlify` CLI on this computer, **new** site, draft deploy | If CLI missing: `npm i -g netlify-cli` then `netlify login`. |

If a connector needs auth, start its connect flow and keep working on research. If OAuth redirect is broken, do **not** loop auth: use the CLI/browser workaround in the table and say so.

Install once if missing:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.grok/bin:$HOME/.treg/bin:$PATH"
command -v grok || curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash
command -v treg || (curl -fsSL https://treg.to/install.sh | sh)
command -v netlify || npm i -g netlify-cli
grok --version; treg --version; netlify --version; gh auth status
```

Grok sign-in: the owner's X account via `grok login --oauth` (hand desktop). Do not paste keys.

## 3. SERP + keyword map

Follow the local keyword-map recipe (80+ candidates, 25+ manual grades, symptoms required). National KD is **not** local difficulty. City phrases below a tool floor = unverified, not zero.

Grade:
- GREEN: weak map pack, directories, or out-of-market doorway in top 5
- YELLOW: 1–2 real local sites
- RED: exact-match locals + stacked LSAs. If head is RED on LSA + maps + organic, pivot the **money** terms, still ship long-tails and the site.

Files: `discovery.md`, `matrix.csv`, `keyword-map.md`, `competitors.md`.

## 4. Aggressive organic plan (always)

Write `RANK-PLAN.md` + print HTML/PDF. Each strategy is H2 + numbered steps:

**A. GBP** (skip only if rank-and-rent): claim, categories, NAP lock, photos, website field after preview, posts.
**B. Reviews:** if rating + count exist, compute extra 5-stars to average A: `n = (N*A − S) / (5 − A)` where `S = current_avg * N`. Report 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5 / 4.0 and a **recency** target (30–50 genuine 5-stars in 30 days after claim + replies on last 50 negatives). Never buy, gate, or fake reviews. QR + verbal ask + SMS after paid job.
**C. Site** (this skill's Grok Build).
**D. On-page / AEO:** follow §4D on every money, city, and FAQ URL. Also: one H1, FAQPage + LocalBusiness JSON-LD, speakable NAP, sitemap, GSC.
**E. Citations:** identical NAP. Real Facebook Page if the Place page is unofficial.
**F. 30/60/90 calendar.**
**G. Do-nots.**

If maps is poisoned by a 2.x average, say so: **rank the website first**; all-time 4.0 can take years.

### 4D. Perfect AEO page checklist (every indexed money page)

Adapted from Nectiv's *Perfectly Optimized Page for AEO* (nectivdigital.com/blog/the-perfectly-optimized-page-for-aeo-ai-search). Local rules override generic blog advice (no invented stats, no fake "last updated").

1. **AI accessibility:** allow GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot in robots.txt unless the client forbids; server-render answer copy (static HTML/SSR); no SPA shells for money pages.
2. **Key takeaways in the top third:** 4–6 short sentences under the H1 that answer the page query; each quotable alone (service + city + who + next step).
3. **Hierarchy:** one H1, H2s support it, H3s nested; tables, bullets, numbered lists for costs (labeled estimates), steps, what's included.
4. **Honest freshness:** visible Last updated only when facts change; `dateModified` matches; never stamp today on unchanged copy.
5. **FAQ block:** 4–8 real buyer questions + FAQPage JSON-LD; answers lead with the direct answer.
6. **Fan-out coverage:** cost, timeline, what's included, who it's for, nearby towns actually served, main objection. One URL owns one intent; no city mill.

**AEO QA gate:** for the homepage and every P0 money page, write pass/fail notes in `aeo-qa.md`. Fail = fix before calling the sprint done.

## 5. IA + copy + design.md

Nav default: Home (pillar) · money services · 3–6 city pages · FAQ · Contact. Sticky mobile: primary conversion.

Write `design.md`: conversion over hero. One typeface (Manrope or Geist). No Inter. No stock SUV/handshake hero. No fake testimonials. No star widget that sells a bad rating. Address reviews honestly in FAQ if the listing is ugly.

Full page copy under `content/` for every URL (title, meta, H1, top-third takeaways, body, FAQ, internal links, schema outline, fan-out H2s). Phone/hours TBD until confirmed. Client-facing copy never contains research language (volumes, competitor names, keyword notes). Then the single handoff file from the keyword-map deliverable skill.

## 6. Grok Build the site (mandatory)

Working dir: `/workspace/{slug}/site` (static HTML, crawlable, `netlify.toml`).

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.grok/bin:$PATH"
cd /workspace/{slug}/site
grok -p "$(cat /workspace/{slug}/GROK-SITE-PROMPT.md)" --always-approve --cwd /workspace/{slug}/site
```

Put the entire spec in `GROK-SITE-PROMPT.md`: identity, IA, design.md, conversion, schema, §4D checklist, robots.txt AI-bot rules, no invented NAP/phone/hours/reviews, EXAMPLE inventory labeled. After grok exits, review files against §4D. If it produced nothing, write the static site locally rather than looping.

## 7. Netlify preview (new project)

```bash
cd /workspace/{slug}/site
npx netlify status || npx netlify login   # hand desktop for OAuth
npx netlify sites:create --name "{slug}-preview" --manual
npx netlify deploy --dir .                 # draft only
```

Never `--prod` onto an existing site the owner didn't name. Send the `*.netlify.app` URL.

## 8. Deliver

Chat: verdict (3–6 lines), review math, Netlify URL, AEO QA summary, then attach PDF + zip of `/workspace/{slug}/` (identity, keyword-map, matrix, RANK-PLAN, aeo-qa, design.md, content/, GROK prompt, site source).

## Guardrails
- Never fabricate volumes or review counts.
- Never buy reviews.
- Never invent "last updated" dates or AEO stats.
- Never use a cloud agent for this site.
- Never deploy over the owner's live sites.
- Semrush failing: use Treg. SERP API blocked: continue, mark map pack unverified. GBP quota 0: checklist, not fake stats.

skills.name: Local niche keyword map deliverable
skills.description: Use this when finishing a local niche keyword-map research job so the user gets ONE agent-ready site-build handoff file that includes SEO/IA plus mandatory design/UX specs (so builders don't ship a generic ugly site).
skills.content:
---
name: Local niche keyword map deliverable
description: >-
  Use this when finishing a local niche keyword-map research job so the user
  gets ONE agent-ready site-build handoff file that includes SEO/IA plus
  mandatory design/UX specs (so builders don't ship a generic ugly site).
---
# Single-file site-build handoff deliverable

## When
After completing a local niche keyword research run (NICHE + CITY). Also when the user asks to combine files or prepare a handoff for a site-building agent.

## Audience
The primary reader is **another agent (or human builder) who will implement the website**. Write instructions they can execute without asking follow-ups — covering **SEO/IA and visual quality**.

## Always do this
1. **Ship ONE primary file** named `{NICHE-SLUG}-{CITY-SLUG}-SITE-BUILD-HANDOFF.md`
2. Self-contained. Do not require opening discovery.md / matrix.csv / competitors.md to build.
3. Working research files stay in the project folder for audit only.
4. In chat: attach **only** the handoff file by default.
5. **Design is mandatory.** A handoff that only lists keywords/H1s is incomplete. Always include Design system + per-page wireframes + DoD visual QA.

## Required handoff structure
1. **Handoff brief** — niche, city, geo, GO/NO-GO, positioning
2. **Design system (global)** — brand vibe (3–5 adjectives + anti-patterns), color tokens with hex, typography, spacing / max width / radius, component kit (header, footer, CTA buttons, trust bar, card, FAQ accordion, form), imagery rules, mobile-first rules
3. **Visual DoD / QA checklist** — real hierarchy, no lorem, consistent spacing, WCAG AA contrast, no wall-of-text, hero CTA above fold
4. **Build order** — numbered P1 → P3
5. **Global SEO/IA rules** — one KW → one URL; intent traps; internal linking; geo disambiguation
6. **Page specs** — one block per page: page_slug, suggested_url, page_type, priority, primary/secondary keywords, h1, title_tag, meta_description, funnel_to, internal_links_out, serp_grade, why_beatable, content_must_include, cta, avoid, plus design fields layout_template, sections_in_order, hero (headline, subhead, CTAs, media), above_fold_must_show (3 max), social_proof
7. **IA / nav** — primary nav + footer
8. **Competitor URL patterns to beat**
9. **Watch-outs**
10. **Appendix** — keyword → page_slug table

## Tone
Imperative. Builder should not invent a random theme. Prefer "Use these tokens / this section order" over "make it look professional."

skills.name: Local SEO existing practice
skills.description: use this when the user gives a live local-business URL and wants keyword analysis plus SEO positioning, not a new site from scratch
skills.content:
---
name: Local SEO existing practice
description: >-
  use this when the user gives a live local-business URL and wants keyword
  analysis plus SEO positioning, not a new site from scratch
---
# Local SEO for an existing practice (any niche)

Use this when the user gives a live URL and wants keywords + positioning, not a greenfield site.

## Inputs (require before ranking work)
- Live URL
- NICHE (the service people type)
- CITY (from NAP, not the marketing copy)
- TOOLS: Keyword Planner plus Semrush or Ahrefs if logged in. Never invent volumes.

## Sequence (do not skip)
1. **Site truth.** Sitemap every URL. Diff visible NAP vs schema vs Google vs directories (area code, street, duplicate WordPress/Wix domains, credentials claimed vs real).
2. **SERP truth.** `[service] [city]`, the high-ticket modifier (intensives, emergency, near me), and 3–5 symptom phrases. Grade GREEN/YELLOW/RED with the local rubric (map reviews, doorways, directories). Never use national KD as local difficulty.
3. **One URL per intent.** Keyword → one slug. 301 cannibals. Money pages first, symptom second. No city mill.
4. **Positioning sentence.** Homepage H1 = service + city + the filter (private pay, day rate, specialty). If they already rank #1 for a high-ticket variant, defend that URL; do not dilute it.
5. **90-day scoreboard.** Ticket price × incremental bookings. Track GSC, GBP calls, forms, booked jobs. Not sessions.
6. **Stop rules.** No new URLs until 301s ship. No ads to a fake form or wrong area code. No credential claims a board would dispute.

## Deliverable
One markdown file: verdict, NAP issues, URL keep/merge table, keyword → URL map, competitor notes, 90-day sprint, this same sequence copied so the next business can reuse it.

skills.name: Grok Build
skills.description: Use this when a task is high-token: large code generation, 3D/WebGL work, multi-file refactors, long builds, or anything that would chew a big context window. Run Grok Build (`grok`) on the shared computer instead of generating that work inline.
skills.content:
---
name: Grok Build
description: >-
  Use this when a task is high-token: large code generation, 3D/WebGL work,
  multi-file refactors, long builds, or anything that would chew a big context
  window. Run Grok Build (`grok`) on the shared computer instead of generating
  that work inline.
---
# Grok Build (high-token work)

The shared computer should have xAI **Grok Build**, the `grok` CLI. Heavy generation belongs there, not in the chat turn.

## When to use it
Use Grok Build when the job is **high token**: scaffolding a lot of files, a long refactor, a full page or site build. Quick replies, one-line CSS, deploys, and lookups stay in the normal turn.

## Install (once)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.grok/bin:$PATH"
grok --version
```

## Sign in
Interactive (opens the box browser — hand the desktop to the owner for password/2FA): `grok login --oauth`
Headless/device code: `grok login --device-auth`
Do not ask the owner to paste an API key into chat. If `XAI_API_KEY` is already in the environment, `grok` can use it.

## Run a high-token task
```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.grok/bin:$PATH"
cd /path/to/project
grok -p "the full task" --always-approve --cwd /path/to/project
```
Stream if you need to watch it: add `--output-format streaming-json`.

Put **everything** the job needs in the prompt: paths, constraints, files to touch, what "done" looks like. Grok Build does not see this chat.

## After it finishes
Review the files it changed. Deploy or follow up yourself. Do not redo the same generation inline. If it exits success with zero files, write the output locally instead of looping.

## Do not
- Paste credentials into chat
- Reinstall on every run if `grok --version` already works
- Use Grok Build for a one-line fix
